searchText: <@&1417820113981145228> v1.7.0-alpha.9 is published: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/releases/tag/v1.7.0-alpha.9 ``` if payload_timeliness(store, head.root, timely=False): return False return True ``` Will never understand why people are afraid of `return not payload_timeliness...` Not even mentioning the joining of the last two ifs lol 🙂 It's more difficult to change in the future. Also less readable 😄 <@755590043632140352> how do you feel about this PR? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5125 Maybe not that exact approach, but the idea of it. FYI, I updated the document to reflect the latest `should_build_on_full` behavior. The proof conclusions are unchanged under the assumptions already stated for the relevant properties, but the prose and pseudocode now match the current specs There have been numerous attempts of adding fork aware changes to the main markdown. As far as I know we've never done that before and I consider them clutter that only make the reading harder. Anyway it seems people like them cause they continue popping up in the spec, almost always around `is_parent_full``
